title: F_3 HIP device kernel
description:
Implement the F_3 HIP device kernel for `permanent_bipedal3` on gfx1030, exposed via the FFI shim from T22.

## Background

The kernel is a HIP/ROCm implementation of the bipedal F_3 permanent for $n \le 64$ matrices, suitable for batch-permanent workloads where many independent matrices are computed in parallel on-device. The single-matrix Ryser walk is inherently sequential at the subset level; the GPU win comes from batching across matrices.

Block / grid sizing: one matrix per HIP block; threads within a block cooperate on fold_mul reduction. Bipedal `add`/`sub`/`mul` map directly to wavefront-wide `__ballot`/AND/XOR primitives.

## Success Criteria

- [ ] [hard] `crates/gf2-kernels-hip/hip/permanent/permanent_bipedal3.hip` exists with the device kernel.
- [ ] [hard] On gfx1030, the kernel produces `permanent_bipedal3` values bit-identical to the CPU reference on 100 random matrices for each $n \in \{16, 24, 32, 40\}$.
- [ ] [hard] Kernel signature accepts a batch of `M` matrices and outputs `M` permanents in a single launch.
- [ ] [hard] Tests gated `#[cfg(feature = "hip")]` and `#[ignore = "external: gfx1030 device required"]` (per CLAUDE.md test-tier conventions).
- [ ] [hard] `cargo build -p gf2-kernels-hip --release --features hip` succeeds.
